description: End-to-end intake pipeline eval: red-flag scan -> deflection OR extraction+classification. Runs through app.intake.start_intake(), the actual entry point, not individual modules in isolation.

cases.description: my VPN connection keeps dropping every couple of minutes
excel keeps crashing whenever I try to open a big spreadsheet
I forgot my password and need to get back into my account
the office wifi feels a bit slow today
cases.note: no KB article covers this specific complaint (below deflection threshold), and the text gives no impact/urgency signal at all -> both resolve UNKNOWN -> safe-default escalation (impact->department, urgency->medium) -> P2. This is the deliberate 'ambiguity escalates, never de-escalates' policy from rules_engine.py, not a bug — ambiguous vague reports get more attention, not less.

cases.description: just my monitor has a weird flicker sometimes, not urgent, whenever you get a chance
my laptop screen just went completely black and I need it working urgently for a client call in 20 minutes
our whole team lost access to the shared project folder this morning
cases.note: department impact, urgency unstated -> escalates to medium via safe default -> P2

cases.description: several people on my team are blocked and can't work because the CRM won't load for any of us
the entire company is unable to access email this morning, this is critical
cases.note: matches the outage red-flag pattern ('entire company ... unable') as well as landing on P1 via the rules engine independently (org impact x high urgency) — both paths agreeing is correct, not a conflict. An org-wide critical outage SHOULD trip immediate red-flag escalation rather than wait on LLM extraction.

cases.description: we've detected ransomware on the finance department's file server, files are being encrypted right now
I think there's been a data breach — customer records may have been exposed
hey, quick one when you have time — I think I might have clicked a phishing link earlier, no big deal probably
cases.note: red flag must override even when the USER downplays it ("no big deal", "quick one") — this is exactly the asymmetric-cost case from the architecture doc

cases.description: system is down for everyone, VPN completely unreachable
cases.note: would otherwise match the VPN KB article — red flag must suppress deflection entirely, a security/outage report should never be handed a self-help article instead of escalation
